transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 5.4. The two largest inline tensor families in every prefill protobuf are Constant node value attributes, not initializers: the O(S^2) float16 causal mask on /model/model/Constant_4 (32,768 bytes at S128 rising to 33,554,432 bytes at S4096) and the 56 float16 [1, 8, C - S, 128] zero cache reserves on /Constant_1 through /Constant_111 (65,536 bytes each at S128, 262,144 at S1024 and S4096). Section 5.4 point 1 states the mechanism exactly: T20 forces initializers over 1,024 bytes into external data, but saves with convert_attribute=false, so a Constant attribute bypasses that threshold and stays inside the protobuf. Prefill carries 2,729 Constant nodes and decode 3,399 (section 5.5), so this is also the single largest operator population in both graph kinds.
transformations.title: Rewrite every Constant node as a graph initializer
transformations.transformation: For every Constant node carrying a value tensor attribute, delete the node and append that tensor to graph.initializer under the name the node produced. No consumer edge is rewritten, because the initializer takes over the produced name. This is a pure canonicalization: it changes where a tensor is stored in the protobuf, never its dtype, shape, or bytes.

transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 5.1, the rank-1 finding. 804 of 922 prefill and 1,231 of 1,326 decode shape-defining operator inputs (the watched positions Reshape[1], Slice[1,2,3,4], Expand[1], Tile[1]) are produced by another node rather than by an initializer, a graph input, or a Constant. The raw material is counted by the rank-7 companion: Shape=65 and ConstantOfShape=62 in prefill; Shape=459, ConstantOfShape=91 and Range=6 in decode. Section 5.1's caveat is the reason this pass exists and the reason its result is a measurement rather than a fix: the detector counts unfolded residue, not proven dynamism, and T20 exported with do_constant_folding=false while every boundary dimension is static, so most of these values provably never vary.
transformations.title: Evaluate and replace nodes whose every input is a known constant
transformations.transformation: Walk the node list once in declaration order, which the ONNX specification requires to be topological and which the engine asserts rather than assumes. A node is folded when its operator is in allowed_ops, it carries no subgraph attribute, none of its outputs is a graph output, every one of its inputs is either omitted or an inline initializer of known value, the total declared bytes of those inputs is at most max_input_bytes, and the total declared bytes of the outputs the evaluation produced is at most max_output_bytes. The node is evaluated by onnx.reference.ReferenceEvaluator on a single-node graph whose only tensors are that node's constant inputs, and each output becomes an initializer under the name the node produced. Every node not folded is counted by reason.

transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 5.5, the rank-5 finding: 7,634 prefill and 10,191 decode nodes against a 2,000-node review convention, of which only 254 are MatMul. Pass 2 deletes the nodes it folds but leaves their operands behind as initializers that nothing reads any more -- above all the 2,729 prefill and 3,399 decode tensors pass 1 promoted out of Constant nodes. Those dead initializers are protobuf bytes, and on the T20 graphs they are the bulk of what this pass reclaims. Section 5.5's mitigation and plan section 6.6 both insist that a node-count reduction is only meaningful when it is measured, which is why this pass reports separately what it removed in nodes and in initializer bytes rather than asserting a saving.
transformations.title: Remove nodes and initializers no graph output depends on
transformations.transformation: Compute the set of tensor names transitively required by the graph outputs, keep every node that produces at least one required name, and drop every initializer and value_info entry whose name is not required. Graph inputs are never removed, whether or not any surviving node consumes them, because the public boundary is the frozen T12 contract and its 60 decode inputs and 3 prefill inputs are part of it.

transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 5.4. The rule fires once per prefill graph at S512 and above, on the mask, whose share of the protobuf is 5.6%, 11.5% and 67.4% at S512, S1024 and S4096; and section 5.4 records that the per-tensor rule is blind to the 56 reserves, which are 71.5%, 78.9%, 80.5% and 29.5% of the four prefill files and are the largest inline family at three of the four variants. Both families are inline only because they were Constant attributes; once pass 1 has made them initializers, the same 1,024-byte threshold that T20 already applies to weights applies to them.
transformations.title: Write initializers at or above the threshold into the candidate sidecar
transformations.transformation: Serialize the candidate with ONNX external-data conversion at size_threshold bytes into one sidecar per candidate graph, named <graph_kind>.onnx.data next to the candidate protobuf. The candidate never shares, references, or modifies the reference graph's sidecar. Node attributes are not converted, because after pass 1 there is no attribute tensor left worth converting.

transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 6 and 7. R-INTERNAL-DYNAMIC-SHAPE is the one silent rule that is explicitly not a clean result: value_info is empty in all eight graphs, so the detector inspected 0 of 0 entries. Section 7 names this pass as the follow-up that closes the boundary, in these words: run ONNX shape inference on a machine with onnx installed, write the inferred value_info back, and re-run the inspection, and the same rule then produces a real answer. Section 3 point 3 records the second cost of the same absence: every intermediate dtype in the T21 report had to be reconstructed by resolve_element_types from opset-18 type constraints rather than read from a declaration.
transformations.title: Run ONNX shape inference and keep the inferred value_info
transformations.transformation: Run onnx.shape_inference on the candidate and keep the value_info entries it produced. The engine then counts how many of the graph's intermediate tensors carry an entry and how many of those entries are fully static, and records both numbers. Inference that annotates only part of the graph is reported as partial with the exact fraction; the pass never claims coverage it did not achieve.

transformations.observed_issue: graph-inspection.md 2 records that the producer string in every one of the eight reference graphs is pytorch 2.7.1 and the IR version is 8. A rewritten candidate that kept that producer string would be indistinguishable in-band from the reference export it was derived from, and the only thing separating the two stages would be the directory it happened to be written to.
transformations.title: Record the source digest, catalogue identity, and applied passes in-band
transformations.transformation: Set producer_name and producer_version to this engine and its schema version, and set metadata_props to the task id, the stage, the variant id, the graph kind, the source graph relative path and sha256, the transform catalogue id and sha256, and the ordered list of applied pass ids. The graph body, the IR version, and the opset imports are left exactly as the preceding passes produced them.
